cards.front: star
cards.back: A huge ball of hot gas that gives out light. The Sun is our star.
cards.say: star. A huge ball of hot gas that gives out light. The Sun is our star.

cards.front: The Sun is a star or a planet?
cards.back: A star.
cards.say: The Sun is a star or a planet? A star.

cards.front: Earth is a star, a planet or a moon?
cards.back: A planet.
cards.say: Earth is a star, a planet or a moon? A planet.

cards.front: The Moon is a star, a planet or a moon?
cards.back: A moon, because it orbits the Earth.
cards.say: The Moon is a star, a planet or a moon? A moon, because it orbits the Earth.

cards.front: orbit
cards.back: The path of one object around another in space.
cards.say: orbit. The path of one object around another in space.

cards.front: What does the Earth orbit?
cards.back: The Sun.
cards.say: What does the Earth orbit? The Sun.

cards.front: What does the Moon orbit?
cards.back: The Earth.
cards.say: What does the Moon orbit? The Earth.

cards.front: How long does the Earth take to orbit the Sun?
cards.back: One year, about 365 and a quarter days.
cards.say: How long does the Earth take to orbit the Sun? One year, about 365 and a quarter days.

cards.front: How long does the Moon take to orbit the Earth?
cards.back: About a month, between 27 and 29 days.
cards.say: How long does the Moon take to orbit the Earth? About a month, between 27 and 29 days.

cards.front: rotate (spin)
cards.back: To turn around an axis.
cards.say: rotate (spin). To turn around an axis.

cards.front: How long does the Earth take to spin once?
cards.back: One day, 24 hours.
cards.say: How long does the Earth take to spin once? One day, 24 hours.

cards.front: What causes day and night?
cards.back: The Earth spins, so each place faces the Sun and then faces away.
cards.say: What causes day and night? The Earth spins, so each place faces the Sun and then faces away.

cards.front: When it is day where you live, what is it on the other side of the Earth?
cards.back: Night.
cards.say: When it is day where you live, what is it on the other side of the Earth? Night.

cards.front: Which way does the Earth spin?
cards.back: From west to east.
cards.say: Which way does the Earth spin? From west to east.

cards.front: Does the Sun really move across the sky?
cards.back: No. It only looks like it moves because the Earth spins.
cards.say: Does the Sun really move across the sky? No. It only looks like it moves because the Earth spins.

cards.front: Where does the Sun appear to rise?
cards.back: In the east.
cards.say: Where does the Sun appear to rise? In the east.

cards.front: Where does the Sun appear to set?
cards.back: In the west.
cards.say: Where does the Sun appear to set? In the west.

cards.front: Does the Moon make its own light?
cards.back: No. It reflects light from the Sun.
cards.say: Does the Moon make its own light? No. It reflects light from the Sun.

cards.front: phases of the Moon
cards.back: The different shapes of the Moon we see through the month.
cards.say: phases of the Moon The different shapes of the Moon we see through the month.

cards.front: Why does the Moon seem to change shape?
cards.back: We see different amounts of its sunlit side as it orbits the Earth.
cards.say: Why does the Moon seem to change shape? We see different amounts of its sunlit side as it orbits the Earth.

cards.front: What is a full moon?
cards.back: When we see the whole sunlit face of the Moon.
cards.say: What is a full moon? When we see the whole sunlit face of the Moon.

cards.front: What is a new moon?
cards.back: When we cannot see the lit side of the Moon.
cards.say: What is a new moon? When we cannot see the lit side of the Moon.

cards.front: How long is a day?
cards.back: 24 hours.
cards.say: How long is a day? 24 hours.

cards.front: True or false: The Sun moves around the Earth.
cards.back: False. The Earth moves around the Sun.
cards.say: True or false: The Sun moves around the Earth. False. The Earth moves around the Sun.

cards.front: Why is a shadow long in the morning?
cards.back: The Sun is low in the sky.
cards.say: Why is a shadow long in the morning? The Sun is low in the sky.
